    wayu CLI reference

    wayu                                   # interactive TUI
wayu <command> [<action>] [arguments] [flags]

    Every command, action word, command flag and --json support listed here comes from one table in the source, WAYU_COMMAND_SPECS (src/wayu_completions.odin), which also drives dispatch, wayu help and wayu's own shell completions. tests/unit/test_cli_doc.odin fails when this file misses a command, alias, action or flag from that table, and tests/integration/test_exit_codes.rb runs the exit code examples below.

    The config file format is described in config-reference.md; behavior changes between releases in UPGRADING.md.

    • Global flags
    • Where flags are recognised
    • Commands
    • JSON output
    • Exit codes
    • Environment variables

    Global flags#

    Flag Meaning
    --dry-run, -n Show what would change; write nothing
    --yes, -y Confirm a destructive operation (see below)
    --json Machine-readable output; only where listed in JSON output, elsewhere exit 64
    --no-color, --no-colour No ANSI escape codes (same as NO_COLOR=1)
    --shell <zsh|bash|fish> Act on this shell's files instead of the one detected from $SHELL
    --full, -f path/alias/const list: include external entries (same as --source all); elsewhere exit 64
    --source <filter>, --source=<filter> path/alias/const list: wayu (default), inactive, external or all; elsewhere exit 64
    --tui Open the TUI (same as running wayu with no arguments)
    --help, -h, help Global help, or a command's help after the command (wayu path --help)
    --version, -v, version Print wayu vX.Y.Z
    -- End of flags: every later word is a literal argument

    --yes is required by path clean, path dedup, backup restore, backup remove, plugin remove, function remove, script remove and config scan --fix whenever they would change something, and always by doctor --fix (unless --dry-run); without it they print what would happen and exit 64.

    Developer flags (golden-file tests, see AGENTS.md): -c=<component> (only before any command word), --test, --snapshot (only with -c=; else exit 64). Their width=N / height=N must be 1-1000 (else exit 64).

    Human-readable output never prints a control character from your data raw: in path/alias/const list, plugin list/get/search, script list, search and doctor, a tab is shown as \t, a newline as \n, other control characters (C0, DEL) and bytes that are not valid UTF-8 as \xHH, and C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F) as \u00HH. --json output and const get, alias get, path get print values exactly as stored.

    An action that takes no arguments (list, secrets lock, toml validate, every export mode, ...) exits 64 on an extra word after it.

    Where flags are recognised#

    1. -- ends flag parsing. Everything after it is a literal argument and the -- itself is dropped: wayu alias add g -- -n stores -n.
    2. In alias add and constants add (const, env), once the name and the first value word have been given, the rest of the line is the value, dashes included: wayu alias add gpf git push -f stores git push -f. Flags may still come before the first value word (wayu alias add -n gc 'git commit'). A dash word right where the value starts is the value: wayu const add OFFSET -5. Exception: --dry-run, --yes, --json and --no-color (and, for constants add, --secret) at the very end of the line are flags (wayu alias add gpf git push -f --dry-run previews). To keep them in the value, put -- before it: wayu alias add hd -- helm install --dry-run. A trailing -n or -y stays in the value with a warning on stderr.
    3. Anywhere else a global flag may appear in any position.
    4. Any other -x / --xyz word must be a flag of that command (listed per command below), else wayu exits 64 (Unknown option) before doing anything — a typo like --dryrun never performs a real write. A word like -5 is a number, not a flag (plugin priority NAME -5).

    Commands#

    An action word a command doesn't have exits 64 with that command's help. wayu <command> help (or -h / --help) prints the command's help. A get / rm of a name that does not exist exits 65 and lists similar names on stderr; it never acts on a guess.

    wayu path#

    Manage PATH entries (stored in <data>/entries.json, see config-reference.md). Default action: list.

    Action Arguments
    add <dir> or <key>=<dir> Add a directory (must exist, else exit 66; a file that is not a directory exits 65; ~ and relative paths are resolved). The key defaults to the directory's base name; an existing directory is left as is (exit 0)
    remove, rm <dir-or-key> Remove an entry by directory or key
    list, ls List entries (--json, --full, --source)
    get <dir> Print the entry (exact directory)
    clean Remove entries whose directory no longer exists (--yes)
    dedup Remove duplicate entries (--yes)
    help 
    wayu path add ~/.cargo/bin
wayu path list --full
wayu path clean --dry-run

    wayu alias#

    Manage aliases (stored in entries.json). Default action: list. Names: printable ASCII except whitespace, quotes, $ ` \ = / ^ ; & | < > ( ) { } [ ] * ? # ~ !, not starting with - (so .., g.st, 1x, k8s-ctx work). Command names may be aliased (alias add cd z); shell grammar words (if, do, function, ...), declaration builtins (local, export, typeset, return, ...), . and names starting with _wayu (wayu's own helpers) are refused (exit 65). The same rule applies to names in entries.json.

    Action Arguments
    add <name> <command...> Add or replace an alias
    remove, rm <name>
    list, ls --json, --full, --source
    get <name> Print the alias's command
    help

    wayu constants (const, env)#

    Manage constants: exported environment variables (stored in entries.json). Default action: list. Names: ASCII letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit. Protected names exit 65: PATH, path, FPATH, fpath, HOME, IFS, SHELL, USER, LOGNAME, PWD, OLDPWD, ZDOTDIR, SHLVL, _, every WAYU_* name (setting them from wayu breaks the shell or wayu), and names whose value a shell runs as code or loads code from: PS0-PS4, PROMPT, prompt, PROMPT2-PROMPT4, RPROMPT, RPROMPT2, RPS1, RPS2, SPROMPT, PROMPT_EOL_MARK, PROMPT_COMMAND, BASH_ENV, ENV, fish_function_path, fish_complete_path. wayu doctor reports stored ones as an error. A value (alias command, constant value, PATH dir) with a NUL byte or invalid UTF-8 exits 65.

    Action Arguments
    add <NAME> <value...> Add or replace a variable
    add <NAME> [value...] --secret Store the value encrypted (see wayu secrets)
    remove, rm <NAME> Plain or encrypted
    list, ls --json, --full, --source, --reveal
    get <NAME> Print the real value (exact name only; decrypts a secret)
    help
    Flag
    --reveal list: show secret-looking values instead of ******** (never encrypted ones)
    --secret add: encrypt the value into secrets.json instead of storing it in entries.json
    --run-only add: like --secret, but the shell never exports it; only the secrets run action injects it

    get is safe in scripts: X=$(wayu const get NAME) either gets that variable's value or fails with exit 65, also when entries.json marks NAME secret but secrets.json has no value for it (wayu doctor reports that as an error, and a value in secrets.json with no secret entry in entries.json as a warning).

    add --secret: without a value, it is read from stdin (hidden when stdin is a terminal; one trailing newline is dropped), so it stays out of argv and shell history: wayu const get OLD | wayu const add NEW --secret. A value given as an argument is accepted with a warning on stderr (other local users can read argv with ps, and it lands in shell history). Like --dry-run, a --secret at the end of the line is a flag, not part of the value. An existing plain constant is converted (its entries.json entry keeps its place, without the value). A plain add of a name that is a secret exits 65; --secret on any other action exits 64 (--run-only likewise). Hooks receive an empty {value} for secrets. list shows secrets as ******** with source wayu (secret) (wayu (secret, inactive) when not in this shell's environment; the same strings in --json), run-only ones with wayu (run-only). Re-adding a secret with --secret or --run-only switches its mode.

    wayu search (find, f)#

    wayu search <query>: fuzzy search over PATH entries (directory or key; the result shows the directory), alias names and constant names (never values: not alias commands, not constant values). Results show the value, masked like const list; an encrypted constant shows ********. Match types: exact, prefix, substring, acronym (first letters of the words: faak → FIREWORKS_AI_API_KEY), fuzzy. Supports --json. Without a query it prints its help and exits 64.

    wayu completions#

    Completion scripts in the data dir's completions/. Default action: list.

    Action Arguments
    add <name> <file> Copy a completion script in
    remove, rm <name>
    list, ls
    generate Write wayu's own zsh, bash and fish completions
    zsh, bash, fish Print wayu's completion script for that shell
    fpath [list], add <dir>, rm <dir> zsh: completion dirs wayu puts on fpath before compinit (entries.json fpath; wayu optimize fills it). add puts the dir first; a dir with :, a newline or a glob character (* ? [ ] ( ) < > | # ^ ~, except a leading ~) is refused
    help

    wayu's own completions parse the line rather than count positions: global flags (with their values) may come anywhere, command flags complete at any position after the command, and -- ends the flags. Besides commands, actions and flags they offer the values of --shell, --source, --lang, --category/-c, --template, existing entries for rm/get/... , backup list|restore|rm types and backup restore <type> numbers, template apply and plugin add names, secrets run secret names and, after --, the command. Run generate again after upgrading wayu.

    wayu backup#

    Default action: list. wayu backs a file up before changing it (once per command) and keeps the newest 5 per file in backup/.

    Action Arguments
    list, ls [type] All backup groups (wayu.toml, entries.json, plugins.json, the rc file, …); --json
    restore <type> [N|file] Restore the file type names from the newest backup, backup #N, or a file (--yes)
    remove, rm [type] Prune to the newest 5 (--yes)
    help

    type is toml (wayu.toml) or entries (entries.json); path, alias and constants also name entries.json, so a restore reverts all PATH entries, aliases and constants together. A shell startup file (zsh, bash or fish; what wayu optimize rewrites) is named as backup list shows it (.zshrc, ~/.config/zsh/.zshrc) or by its path. The current file is backed up first.

    Each entries.json backup keeps a copy of secrets.json (ciphertext only) as it was at that moment, in backup/secrets/; restoring entries.json restores secrets.json with it (or removes it when there was none), so secret constants and their values stay paired. Backups without that copy (taken before this, or before a secrets rekey, which drops the copies: their values were encrypted with the old key) restore entries.json only.

    wayu plugin#

    Default action: list. <name> must match an installed plugin exactly.

    Action Arguments
    add <registry-key-or-git-url> Clone and enable a plugin
    remove, rm <name> Uninstall (--yes)
    list, ls --json
    get <name> Show details
    search [query] Browse the built-in registry
    enable, disable <name>
    priority <name> <number> Load order, lower first (default 100)
    check Check for updates
    update <name> or --all Fast-forward to the remote
    help
    Flag
    --all, -a update: every plugin
    --category <c>, -c <c>, --category=<c> search: filter by category
    --use <glob>, --use=<glob> add: file(s) to load from the repository root (repeatable)

    wayu init#

    wayu init [--template <name>]: create the config dir (~/.config/wayu) and the data dir (${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/wayu), a wayu.toml scaffold and init.<ext>, generate the init files, and offer to add this line to your rc file (only when stdin is a terminal; otherwise it prints the line):

    source "${WAYU_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/wayu}/init.zsh"

    Safe to re-run: existing files are kept and an unmodified init.<ext> from the previous release is updated. --shell picks the shell.

    Flag
    --template <name>, --template=<name> Then apply a template (see wayu template list)

    wayu config#

    Without an action it prints its help.

    Action
    edit Open wayu.toml in $VISUAL / $EDITOR (else vi), then regenerate
    extend Open extra.<ext> (shell code sourced at the end of init)
    scan Find tool-init blocks in the current shell's rc file (zsh: $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc when set) that could move to extra.<ext>, including # >>> … # <<< installer blocks
    help
    Flag
    --fix scan: append the blocks found to extra.<ext> of the same shell (--yes); the rc file is left as is (wayu optimize moves lines and removes them)

    wayu build#

    Action
    (none) Regenerate the init files from wayu.toml and entries.json (after a hand edit), and plugins.<ext> from plugins.json, for every set-up shell. Exit 78 when plugins.json is invalid (the plugin loaders are left as they were; everything else is regenerated) or a [tools] entry's args is unusable
    turbo Same as wayu export --turbo
    profile Time shell startup and each section, tool and plugin of core.<ext>. core is timed in an interactive shell whose only rc file sources it (zsh: ZDOTDIR set to a private temp dir; bash: --rcfile; fish: -i --no-config), so compinit, the prompt and plugins count; the per-unit breakdown needs zsh or bash 5+
    clean Delete the [tools] evalcache (${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/wayu/evalcache)
    help

    wayu export#

    Default action: turbo. Each action may also be written as a flag (--turbo, --eval, --check).

    Action
    turbo Write turbo.<ext>, a copy of core.<ext> (fish: core.fish followed by tools.fish and extra.fish, like init.fish)
    eval Print constants, PATH entries and aliases as shell code for eval "$(wayu export --eval)" (fish: wayu export --eval | source; writes nothing). Keep the double quotes: an unquoted eval $(…) glob-expands the output against the current directory, so a crafted file name there can run code
    check Exit 0 if turbo.<ext> is current — its content is exactly what export --turbo would write now (any input: wayu.toml, entries.json, config.<ext>, a newer wayu) — 78 if it is missing or stale
    list, ls Show the formats
    help

    wayu toml#

    Action
    validate Strict check of wayu.toml (syntax, duplicate keys, [shell] type, table shapes, no [paths] / [aliases] / [env]); exit 65 on error. Keys wayu does not read are warnings (exit 0)
    show Print wayu.toml
    keys List wayu.toml's top-level keys and tables, in file order; exit 65 if it does not parse
    help

    Without an action, wayu toml behaves like wayu toml validate.

    wayu doctor#

    Health checks: installation, rc file, PATH entries, plugins and plugin conflicts, backups, wayu.toml (a [paths], [aliases] or [env] table is an error naming the wayu path|alias|const add command), entries.json (must parse), scripts (error: two sources for one name or a CRLF shebang; warning: stale or broken builds), script bin entries (bin/ entries without a script; --fix removes them), turbo file, dependencies, startup files (lines wayu optimize would move, a second compinit counts ~250 ms; generator commands are listed, never run: doctor does not execute rc file content), directory permissions (a config/data dir, or a subdir of them two levels deep, symlinks not followed, that is group- or other-writable is an error: another user could change startup code or put commands in bin/; wayu creates its dirs 0700 whatever the umask). Exits 78 when any check reports an error (warnings don't), so it can gate CI. Supports --json.

    Flag
    --fix Remove missing / duplicate PATH entries, run wayu optimize, remove group/other write from wayu dirs (--yes, or --dry-run to preview)
    --profile Write a zsh startup profiler script to <data>/startup_profile.zsh (see also wayu build profile); exits 64 with --json or --fix
    --optimize Removed; prints a pointer to wayu build / wayu export and exits 64

    wayu template#

    Default action: list. Templates: developer, minimal, data-science, full.

    Action Arguments
    list, ls
    apply <name> Add the template's entries; existing ones are kept, PATH dirs missing on this machine (or not directories) are skipped
    help

    wayu hooks#

    Default action: list. Hooks are configured in hooks.conf (config-reference.md).

    Action
    list, ls Show configured hooks
    edit Open hooks.conf in the editor
    help

    Hooks run outside wayu's config lock (so they may run wayu), with their output shown, and are killed after 30 s (timeout in hooks.conf).

    wayu function (functions, func, fn)#

    Shell functions as files in the data dir's functions/ (sourced by core.<ext>, so they can change the shell's state). Default action: list.

    Action Arguments
    add, new, edit <name> Create (from a skeleton for the shell, mode 0600) or open the function file in the editor; without $EDITOR / $VISUAL and a terminal, print its path instead. A dangling symlink at the path exits 73
    list, ls
    remove, rm, delete <name> Delete the file (--yes)
    help

    wayu script (scripts)#

    Standalone executables in any language, on PATH. Sources live in the data dir's scripts/ (the directory is the list: NAME.<ext>); what runs is bin/NAME, and core.<ext> puts the data dir's bin/ first among wayu's PATH entries (once it holds a script) in zsh, bash and fish. Interpreted scripts are linked (bin/NAME → ../scripts/NAME.<ext>, source 0755); compiled ones are built into bin/NAME (swift: swiftc -O, or any build command a source declares, below). Default action: list.

    Action Arguments
    new <name> [--lang <lang>] Create scripts/<name>.<ext> from a skeleton, open it in the editor, build it. Exit 65 if the name exists or anything (a symlink too) is at that path
    edit <name> Open the source in the editor, then rebuild it if it changed
    list, ls Name, language, state, source; --json
    remove, rm <name> Delete the source (backed up first) and its bin/ entry (--yes); a bin/ entry without a script is removed alone
    import <file>... Move existing scripts in (--copy keeps the originals; --allow-build runs build commands they declare; --dry-run previews)
    build [<name>...] Build every stale script, or the ones named
    help
    Flag
    --lang <lang>, --lang=<lang> new: swift, python, ruby, node (.js), bun (.ts), bash, zsh, fish, perl, lua, sh. Default: [scripts] default_lang in wayu.toml, else swift. An unknown value exits 64
    --copy import: keep the original files
    --allow-build import: import files that declare their own build command (below), which wayu then runs now and on every rebuild. Without it such a file makes import exit 64 before anything is imported or run (a language preset such as swift's swiftc -O -o {out} {src} needs no flag)

    Names: ASCII letters, digits, _, and - after the first character.

    new writes a shebang with the absolute path of the interpreter found on PATH at that moment (#!/opt/homebrew/bin/python3); when it is missing (for swift: swiftc) it exits 69 naming it. Without $EDITOR / $VISUAL and a terminal it prints the new file's path instead of opening an editor.

    Build commands: a source in any language may declare how it is built in a comment line (//, #, --, ;, /*, *) among its first 20 lines:

    // wayu: build = cc -O2 -o {out} {src}

    {src} is the source, {out} the file the command must write (it becomes bin/NAME; a command without {out} is refused). The words are split like a shell would (quotes, backslashes; no expansions or pipes) and run without a shell, in the data dir's scripts/ (never the directory wayu was started in); the first word is looked up on PATH. Such a source may have any extension (tool.c → tool). Swift's swiftc -O -o {out} {src} is the same mechanism as a preset, used when a swift source declares none.

    Python with inline dependencies (PEP 723) runs through uv without a build: give the script the shebang #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script and a # /// script block (it is a python script: uv in a shebang is recognised on import):

    #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# dependencies = ["requests"]
# ///
import requests

    Two sources with the same name (foo.sh, foo.rb) are an error: neither is built (script build exits 1), edit / build / rm of that name exit 65, and doctor reports it. A source whose shebang line ends in CR (CRLF line endings; it could only fail with bad interpreter) is not linked and doctor reports it; import converts such a file to LF.

    A compiled script is stale when its source or build command no longer matches the hash stored in bin/.NAME.hash (or the binary is missing); an interpreted one when its link is missing or wrong. wayu build, wayu reload (which also watches the sources) and script build rebuild stale scripts (the wayu build that the prompt hook runs starts a background script build instead of waiting for the compiler). A failed compile prints the compiler's output, exits 1 and keeps the previous binary.

    import takes regular text files with a #! line, a known extension or a build command header. The language comes from the shebang's interpreter (#!/usr/bin/env X is read as X, skipping env's options and their arguments: -u VAR, -P dir, -C dir, --unset=VAR; trailing version digits are ignored: python3.12 → python), else from the extension. The file keeps its shebang and a known extension (else gets the language's); a file without a shebang gets one for the interpreter on PATH. It skips, with the reason: symlinks, binaries (NUL byte or Mach-O/ELF header in the first 4 KiB), launchers generated by package managers (shebang inside a venv, pipx or uv tool dir, or a console_scripts stub from X import F … sys.exit(F())), wrappers whose only command is exec "/abs/path" "$@" (launcher for /abs/path), unknown interpreters and names that already exist. A file with a wayu: build = header shows the command ([build: …]) in --dry-run and in the summary; unless it is a language preset it needs --allow-build. Each file is copied and built before the original is removed; one that fails to build is skipped and left in place. A summary lists what was imported and skipped; exit 65 when nothing was imported.

    wayu script new hello --lang python
wayu script import ~/bin/* --dry-run
wayu script list --json

    wayu secrets (secret)#

    Encrypted constants. wayu const add NAME [VALUE] --secret stores the value encrypted (ChaCha20-Poly1305, AAD = the name) in the data dir's secrets.json (0600); the 256-bit master key lives in the [secrets] backend (macOS keychain, Secret Service, or secret.key in the config dir). const get decrypts, const rm removes. Default action: list.

    Action Arguments
    list, ls Secret names and mode (session or run-only), one per line (never values)
    rekey New master key, re-encrypt every secret, drop the session cache
    lock Delete the decrypted session cache from every dir it was written to (next shell decrypts again)
    run <NAME>... -- <cmd> [args...] Run cmd with these secrets in its environment
    identity [--name NAME] (experimental) Print this machine's age recipient (age1…) on stdout, creating its identity the first time; stderr shows the recipient add command to run on a machine that reads the secrets (--name: the name in that command, default hostname -s; NAME when the hostname is empty or an IP address)
    recipient list (ls) [--json] · add <age1…> [--name NAME] · rm <NAME> --yes · rename <OLD> <NEW> (experimental) Machines that can read the secrets (see below)
    adopt --yes (experimental) Accept the data key in this machine's stanza without a rotation proof: a new machine's first step (prints the fingerprint to compare). Never a key this machine replaced. On a version 1 file this machine knew as version 2: back to one machine
    recovery add [--name NAME] · rm --yes · unlock (experimental) Recovery passphrase (read from stdin, never argv)
    help

    Run-only secrets. wayu const add NAME [VALUE] --run-only stores a secret that shells never export: it is not in the session cache, core.<ext>, turbo.<ext> or export --eval. wayu secrets run NAME... -- CMD [ARGS...] decrypts the named secrets (run-only or not) and replaces itself with CMD (looked up on PATH, no shell, no extra process), its environment being wayu's plus those variables, so the exit status and signals are CMD's own. Values are never printed; --dry-run prints the names and the command. Exit 64 without --, names or a command; 65 for a name that is not a secret; 127 when CMD is not found; 126 when it cannot be executed. The run-only mark is bound into the encryption (AAD), so editing it out of secrets.json makes the value undecryptable instead of exporting it. Typical use, an alias that gives one tool its token:

    wayu const add GH_TOKEN --run-only            # value from stdin
wayu alias add gh 'wayu secrets run GH_TOKEN -- gh'

    Shells never read plaintext from the data dir: core.<ext> sources a per-login-session cache, ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-<data>/run}}/wayu-<uid>/secrets-<id>.<ext> (0600 in a 0700 dir owned by you; <data>/run/wayu-<uid> when that dir is a symlink, not yours, or open to group/other; a symlinked cache file is never sourced), when it is newer than secrets.json; otherwise it runs wayu secrets cache once (a hidden helper that decrypts into that file). When the key is unavailable or a value does not decrypt, the shell prints one wayu: secrets not loaded: … line on stderr and starts without the secrets. The first add --secret creates the key; wayu never creates a new key while secrets.json holds values (exit 78). Errors reading the store or key exit 78; write errors 74.

    Multi-machine secrets (experimental)#

    The same secrets.json (with entries.json) can be read on several machines without copying any key between them. Each machine has its own age X25519 identity (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…, kept by the [secrets] backend), and secrets.json version 2 wraps one data key to every machine's recipient (age1…); see config-reference.md. Experimental: these actions and the version 2 format may change in a minor release (a format change still migrates automatically). The first use prints a one-time notice on stderr.

    wayu secrets identity                              # on the new machine B: prints age1…
wayu secrets recipient add age1… --name linux-box  # on machine A: prints the data key fingerprint
# sync secrets.json (and entries.json) to B, then on B:
wayu secrets adopt --yes                           # prints the same fingerprint: compare them
    • recipient add <age1…> [--name NAME] needs the data key. The first one upgrades a version 1 store to version 2 (backup first, then a verify step; a one-time notice says wayu 7.0 cannot read it): the master key becomes the data key unchanged, this machine is added as hostname -s, value lines are untouched. --name is required for another machine's key (default hostname -s for this machine's own; when the hostname is empty or an IP address there is no default: 64, add this machine first with wayu secrets recipient add "$(wayu secrets identity)" --name NAME). It prints the data key's fingerprint (data key fingerprint: …) and, for another machine, the adopt step to run there. 65: bad or reserved recipient (post-quantum age1pq1… is reserved, not supported), bad name, duplicate name or recipient. 64: missing --name for another machine.
    • recipient rm <NAME> --yes drops the machine and always rotates: a new data key, every value re-encrypted, re-wrapped to the remaining recipients, a rotation proof appended, the session cache and backup copies of secrets.json dropped. The removed machine can no longer read values stored from then on (it already decrypted the old ones: rotate those credentials upstream). Machines that have not synced since the rm are exposed until they do: the removed machine still holds the old key and can sign a rotation from it, which such a machine accepts. The recovery passphrase survives rm: if the removed machine knew it, replace it (recovery rm --yes, then recovery add; rm says so). Removing this machine or the last recipient is refused (65). Without --yes: 64. An entry that fails the stanza check is dropped before the check runs on the rest, so the rm an error names always works.
    • recipient rename <OLD> <NEW>, recipient list [--json] (marks this machine; also prints the data key's fingerprint).
    • rekey on a version 2 store makes a new data key, wraps it to every recipient and appends a rotation proof.
    • Each machine caches the data key it verified in the backend's existing master-key item, with what it verified (local state: that it read version 2, the recipients, the ones it saw removed, the keys it replaced). Shell start uses it while its fingerprint (key_id) matches: no public-key operation, no extra fork. A different key is taken from this machine's stanza only when the rotation proofs (at most 16) chain it to the cached key and it lists no machine this one saw removed; stderr prints adopted data key … (rotation from … verified); recipients: +x, -y. A machine with nothing cached (a new one) takes no key by itself: it exits 78 naming wayu secrets adopt --yes, which prints the fingerprint to compare with the one recipient add printed. An unproven key, or one listing a removed machine again, is also 78 naming adopt: compare the fingerprint with recipient list on another machine first. adopt exits 78 when this machine has no stanza.
    • A secrets.json under a key this machine replaced (an old copy synced back) exits 78 ("older than this machine's data key"): get the current file again; adopt and recovery unlock refuse that key too. A version 1 file on a machine that read version 2 (a downgrade) exits 78 for every read and write: sync the version 2 file again, or, going back to one machine on purpose, adopt --yes (only when every value decrypts with this machine's key).
    • A machine that is not a recipient prints wayu: secrets not loaded: this machine is not a recipient …; run 'wayu secrets identity' and add it from a machine that is at shell start.
    • recovery add sets a passphrase stanza (argon2id; wayu-only, not an age stanza): recovery unlock (passphrase on stdin) recovers the data key on any machine with the file, caches it, and says how to add the machine. recovery rm --yes drops it and rotates. A passphrase shorter than 12 characters, or a wrong one (or a modified salt: "wrong passphrase, or the recovery entry was modified"): 65. argon2id parameters other than the ones wayu writes (64 MiB, 3 passes, 4 lanes): 78, before any work.
    • Every error exits non-zero and names the command that fixes it. --dry-run writes nothing (no identity, no key, no notice marker).

    wayu optimize#

    wayu optimize [--check] [--dry-run] [--yes]: move the lines installers append to your shell startup files into wayu, and remove them from the file. Scanned, in load order, for the current shell (or --shell): zsh ~/.zshenv and $ZDOTDIR (else ~) .zshenv, .zprofile, .zshrc, .zlogin; bash .bash_profile, .bash_login, .profile, .bashrc; fish conf.d/*.fish, config.fish. Only lines after the line that loads wayu, and only top-level statements: anything inside if/for/while/ case/function bodies, here-documents, compound lines and values wayu can't reproduce exactly stays untouched.

    Line Becomes
    source <(tool completion zsh), . <(…), eval "$(tool init zsh)"; fish tool init fish | source A cached generator (entries.json generators): core.<ext> runs _wayu_evalcache tool … (output cached, regenerated when the binary changes; wayu build clean clears it). Only from the interactive file (.zshrc, .bashrc; fish: any), only for a plain command on PATH whose arguments name an init, completion(s), hook, shellenv or activate subcommand; zsh/bash run it in interactive shells only
    fpath=(dir $fpath), fpath+=(dir), FPATH=dir:$FPATH (zsh) entries.json fpath (see wayu completions fpath): on fpath before wayu's compinit
    compinit, autoload -Uz compinit && compinit -C … (zsh) Removed: wayu already runs compinit
    export PATH=dir:$PATH, PATH="$PATH:dir", path=(dir $path); fish set -gx PATH dir $PATH, fish_add_path dir PATH entries, prepends in front of the list (a later line further in front), appends at its end (a dir already listed stays where it is)
    alias name=value (fish also alias name value) An alias; the value must not expand when defined (alias x="cd $HOME" stays)
    export NAME=value; fish set -gx NAME value A constant; a secret-looking name or value is stored encrypted (const add --secret). Values may use $HOME, $USER, ~/ and constants wayu already has

    Without --yes it prints a unified diff per file (a secret constant's lines show as a placeholder, never the value) and the list of what moves, then exits 64; --dry-run prints the same and exits 0. With --yes each changed file is backed up (wayu backup restore .zshrc --yes undoes it; entries.json is backed up too; a moved secret stays in plaintext in that rc backup, which wayu says and never deletes on its own), rewritten atomically, entries.json updated under the config lock and the init files regenerated. A second run finds nothing and exits 0.

    Flag
    --check Write nothing; list the optimizable lines and exit 1 when there are any, 0 when there are none

    Open shells notice changes: the prompt hook compares the startup files' mtimes with <data>/rc_check.stamp (a builtin -nt test, no fork) and, when one is newer, runs wayu optimize --notify once, which prints wayu: ~/.zshrc changed: N lines can be optimized (wayu optimize) on stderr (once per change). With [settings] auto_optimize = true in wayu.toml it moves them instead (with backups) and prints what it moved.

    wayu reload (watch, hot-reload)#

    wayu reload [start|stop|status|regenerate]. start (the default) watches wayu.toml, entries.json and secrets.json and regenerates the init files on change (debounced) until interrupted (a secrets.json change, including the file appearing or going away, also drops the secrets session cache; script sources too: an edit rebuilds the script); stop stops a running watcher; status says whether one runs; regenerate (regen) regenerates once. The running watcher holds a lock on <data>/watcher.lock; stop / status treat a watcher.pid without that lock held as stale (removed, nothing signalled), and start refuses while it is held. stop signals only the process holding the lock, and only when watcher.pid names it (otherwise it exits 1 without signalling). The watcher rebuilds scripts and regenerates under the config lock, like the CLI.

    wayu version#

    Prints wayu vX.Y.Z.

    wayu help#

    Prints the global help: commands, flags, command flags, examples, exit codes.

    JSON output#

    --json is accepted by path|alias|const|plugin|backup|script list, secrets recipient list, search and doctor (and by any help); anywhere else it exits 64. Output is one JSON document on stdout (errors stay on stderr); an empty list is []. The shapes below are checked by tests/integration/test_cli_output.rb — new keys may be added, existing ones keep their meaning.

    Command Document
    path list {"paths": [{"path", "source", "exists": bool}]}
    alias list {"aliases": [{"alias", "command", "source"}]}
    const list {"constants": [{"constant", "value", "source"}]}; an encrypted constant is {"constant", "secret": true, "source"} (no value; source wayu (secret) or wayu (secret, inactive)), plus "run_only": true and source wayu (run-only) for a run-only one
    plugin list {"plugins": [{"name", "enabled": bool, "priority": int, "shell", "url", "commit", "installed_path", "conflicts": [{"kind", "name", "with"}]}], "count": int, "enabled": int}
    backup list {"backups": [{"file", "count": int, "entries": [{"index": int, "timestamp", "size_bytes": int, "path", "pre_restore": bool}]}]}
    script list {"scripts": [{"name", "lang", "source", "bin", "compiled": bool, "stale": bool}], "count": int}
    secrets recipient list {"recipients": [{"name", "recipient", "this_machine": bool}], "key_id", "recovery": bool} (experimental); a version 1 store has "recipients": [] and "key_id": ""
    search QUERY {"query", "results": [{"type", "name", "value", "match", "field", "score": int}], "count": int}; field is always name; an encrypted constant adds "secret": true (its value is "")
    doctor {"checks": [{"name", "status", "message", "fixable": bool}], "summary": {"ok", "warnings", "errors", "info", "fixable"}}

    Unmarked fields are strings. source is wayu, wayu (inactive) (in entries.json but not in this shell's environment) or external; --source and --full filter rows, not the shape. const list masks secret-looking values as ******** unless --reveal is given. Plugin shell is zsh|bash|both|fish|any; a conflict's kind is function|alias|env and with is another plugin or entries.json. Doctor status is ok|warning|error|info; backup list timestamp is ISO 8601 UTC.

    Exit codes#

    BSD sysexits.h values (EXIT_* in src/interfaces.odin):

    Code Name Meaning
    0 EXIT_SUCCESS Success (also: nothing to do)
    1 EXIT_FAILURE General error (e.g. the editor exited non-zero; the TUI started without a terminal); optimize --check: lines can be optimized
    64 EXIT_USAGE Bad usage: unknown command, action or option; missing argument; --json where unsupported; missing --yes
    65 EXIT_DATAERR Bad input: invalid name or value, no such entry, unknown template, toml validate failed
    66 EXIT_NOINPUT Input file or directory not found or unreadable (path add of a missing dir)
    69 EXIT_UNAVAILABLE A required tool is not installed (script new: the language's interpreter or compiler)
    71 EXIT_OSERR TUI: the terminal could not be put in raw mode
    73 EXIT_CANTCREAT Cannot create an output file or directory
    74 EXIT_IOERR Read/write failure, failed git operation
    77 EXIT_NOPERM Permission denied
    78 EXIT_CONFIG Configuration problem: not initialized, invalid hooks.conf, entries.json or plugins.json (build), relative WAYU_CONFIG_DIR / WAYU_DATA_DIR, doctor found an error, export check found no current turbo file
    126 EXIT_EXEC_NOT_RUNNABLE secrets run: the command was found but cannot be executed
    127 EXIT_EXEC_NOT_FOUND secrets run: the command was not found

    Interrupted (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP) while a child process runs (git, a compiler, a profiled shell), wayu kills the child's whole process group, undoes a partial plugin add clone and exits 128 + signal (130 for Ctrl-C, 143 for SIGTERM, 129 for SIGHUP).

    Environment variables#

    Variable Effect
    WAYU_CONFIG_DIR Config dir (wayu.toml, extra/tools, hooks.conf); default ~/.config/wayu. Must be absolute (else exit 78)
    WAYU_DATA_DIR Data dir (entries.json, functions/, scripts/, bin/, plugins, generated init files, completions, backups); default ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/wayu. Must be absolute (else exit 78)
    XDG_DATA_HOME Base of the default data dir (ignored when relative)
    SHELL Shell detection (override with --shell)
    NO_COLOR Disable colors (wins over FORCE_COLOR)
    FORCE_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE Keep colors when stdout is not a terminal
    VISUAL, EDITOR Editor for `config edit
    COLUMNS Table width when not writing to a terminal
    XDG_CACHE_HOME Base of the [tools] evalcache
    WAYU_GIT_TIMEOUT Seconds before a plugin clone/fetch/check is killed
    WAYU_THEME TUI: light or dark (skips background detection)
    ESCDELAY TUI: milliseconds that separate Esc from an Alt+key chord (default 100)
